jobs.description: Employer: American Conservation Experience Expires: 08/13/2026 SummaryAmerican Conservation Experience, a nonprofit Conservation Corps, in partnership with the National Park Service, is seeking ONE Preservation Maintenance Member to assist with the preservation and maintenance of historic structures and landscape alongside the Jimmy Carter NHP Staff.For more information about ACE, please visit our website. Start Date: As soon as possibleEstimated End Date: 52 weeks after start*a 52-week minimum commitment is required * Location Details/Description: Jimmy Carter National Historic Park, Plains, GAThe Jimmy Carter National Historical Park preserves sites associated with James Earl Carter, Jr. (born 1924), 39th president of the United States. These include his residence, boyhood farm, school, and the town railroad depot, which served as his campaign headquarters during the 1976 election. The building which used to be Plains High School (opened in 1921 and closed in 1979) serves as the park & museum and visitor center. Plains is a rural community in Southwest Georgia with full services available in Americus, GA (10 miles); Albany, GA (40 miles); and Columbus, GA (50 miles).For more information about the site, please visit the NPS website.Position Overview: Maintain and preserve all park historic buildings and landscapes in accordance with NPS historical guidelines and Historic structures Reports. Assist NPS Staff in the preservation and maintenance of park structures and assets as well as cultural landscape and historical landscape.Duties may include: Cleaning and inspecting structures and landscapes. Perform painting duties, basic carpentry duties and general maintenance practices under NPS Supervision. Work alongside NPS Maintainers and Gardners to preserve all park historical structure assets.Work with the facilities team to provide support of park maintenance operations (ensuring visitor and administrative areas are clean and safe)Provide support for grounds, custodial, and historic structure repairs (daily cleaning of buildings and restrooms, assist with structure repairs, garden with hand tools, maintain clean landscape)This position is located in Plains, Georgia where the climate has hot, humid summers and in the winter can have cold days. There are insects, bees and wasps, and snakes that inhabit the area as well. The position requires mainly outdoor work dealing with the aforementioned conditions. During inclement weather, you will be provided indoor tasks.This individual placement is meant to facilitate professional development and promotes exposure to land management agencies and networking with professionals. This could include gaining experience in different conservation fields and shadowing different work groups.Schedule: Schedule will be Monday – Friday 7am- 3:30 pm eastern time. Possibility of weekend work during events and special scheduling circumstances.Position BenefitsLiving Allowance: The ACE Member is expected to contribute ~40 hours/week and will receive a living allowance of $650/week (pre-tax) to offset the costs of food and incidental expenses, dispersed bi-weekly.This position is part of the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority: Members serving under this agreement must meet the PLC Eligibility requirements to be considered for this position. Members may be eligible for a federal hiring authority upon completion of their term of service and 640 hours of service. If the duration of a PLC-eligible term is not long enough for Members to accrue 640 hours of service (~16 weeks), the total hours served at the completion of the term may be eligible to be combined with hours accrued from another PLC-eligible term to meet the 640 hours requirement. PLC projects also include specific eligibility requirements such as age (You must be between the ages of 16 and 30. Some agencies also interpret these guidelines to include veterans up to age 35) and citizenship. Required to stoop, kneel, climb stairs, and/or crouch.Vision Requirements: Requires close, distance, peripheral and depth perception vision as well as the ability to focus.Weight Lifted or Force Exerted: Frequently moves up to 20 lbs., ability to move up to 50 pounds.Environmental: Outdoor and indoor conditions. jobs.description: Employer: City of San José - Environmental Services Department Expires: 08/16/2026 The Environmental Services Department (ESD) is a national leader in pollution prevention, watershed protection, utility service provision, and climate action. Together, ESD employees positively impact every resident and business in San Jose. Our department is an exceptional place to start or grow your career. We have a supportive leadership team, numerous professional growth opportunities, and an inclusive workplace culture that is welcoming of your talents! To learn more about ESD, follow @sjenvironment on X (formally Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, and San Jose Environmental Services on LinkedIn. Duration of Assignment:Approximately 1 year with the possibility to extend. Salary ranges for this classification are:Undergraduate Student Intern: $16.33 - $23.33 hourlyGraduate Student Intern: $21.14 - $31.22 hourly These salary ranges include an approximate five percent (5%) ongoing non-pensionable compensation. The intern may also support field work at the San José-Santa Clara Regional Wastewater Facility and within the Water Resources Division. Basic geospatial analysis techniques such as overlay and buffer analysis.Geospatial editing techniques such as erase, divide, minus, and union.Utilizing GNSS-based equipment to capture geospatial data in the field.Subsurface Utility Engineering and Underground Service Alert processes.One or more scripting/programming languages. jobs.description: Employer: LA-Tech.org Expires: 08/16/2026 Spring 2027 Rising Internship — Technical TrackSoftware Engineering · Cybersecurity · IT · AIPaid · 12 Weeks · Los Angeles County · Starting February 2027 Real Work. Real Mentors. A supportive pathway into tech, right here in LA.If you're 18-24, based in Los Angeles County, and ready to build your future in tech, this is for you. The Rising Internship Program - Technical Track is a paid, 12-week experience where you'll work on meaningful projects alongside industry professionals in Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, IT, and AI. You don't need a degree. You don't need to have it all figured out. You need curiosity, commitment, and a drive to grow. This cohort has a high concentration in AI, meaning you'll develop foundational skills in artificial intelligence alongside your core technical track. What Interns GetHands-on project work: Most of your time is spent doing real work on real projects, not sitting through lectures.1-on-1 mentorship: Get matched with a tech professional who's been in your shoes and can help you figure out your next move.A credential that opens doors: Earn credit toward a U.S. Department of Labor-recognized pre-apprenticeship in Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, AI Prompt Engineering, or Project Management. This signals to employers that you're ready for what's next.Interview practice: Sharpen your pitch and walk into your next opportunity with confidence.Industry drop-ins: Tech professionals share what it actually takes to build a career in the field.Career workshops: Learn to tell your story, build your personal brand, and show up strong on LinkedIn and beyond.A supportive peer network across LA: The connections you make here are built to last. This is huge! Spring 2027 Application WindowApplications open: July 2026Deadline: December 2026Internship Start Date: February 2027 Starting an ApplicationBe sure to include your most up-to-date resume and any supporting material under "Upload File" on the official application page. Applications without a resume will not be reviewed. What's RequiredAll participants must be able to:Commit 10-15 hours per week, including asynchronous work.Attend live virtual sessions every Tuesday & Thursday, 4:00-6:30 PM (no early dismissal - please plan accordingly)Attend the in-person intern retreat (date TBD)Attend the in-person tech campus site visit (date TBD)Attend Demonstration Day in person (May 2027) Who Should ApplyRequired Eligibility:Be between the ages of 18 and 24 (*this is a Los Angeles County requirement)Currently reside in Los Angeles or Los Angeles County (proof required if selected*) Able to commit 10-15 hours/week, including mandatory live virtual sessions every Tuesday/Thursday from 4:00-6:30 pm We're looking for young adults who have some exposure to tech concepts — through school, self-study, personal projects, or just genuine curiosity. You don't need to be enrolled in college. We consider a full range of backgrounds and experiences.What matters most: a real interest in tech, a willingness to show up, and a commitment to LA-Tech.org's mission of expanding access to careers in the industry. LocationThe LA Tech Rising Internship operates exclusively in Los Angeles County. Applicants without a Los Angeles-based address are not eligible at this time. All mandatory in-person events will take place at venues across Los Angeles. Wage InformationThis is a paid internship made possible through LA County's Youth@Work Program. Compensation is set at California's minimum wage and is not negotiable. Learn more about the Youth@Work Program here. Why LA-Tech.org?Breaking into tech is hard, especially when you're doing it without a roadmap or a network. LA-Tech.org exists to change that. We connect LA's untapped talent with the tech community because we believe the access gap, not a skills gap, is what holds most people back. If you're ready to put in the work, we'll be with you every step of the way. You belong in tech. Let's build that path together.

jobs.description: Employer: EMI Advisors LLC Expires: 08/17/2026 EMI Advisors LLC (EMI) is a digital transformation firm that operationalizes disruptive technologies for mission impact. We provide end-to-end strategic, operational, and technical advisory services, working with our client partners across health and human services, defense, and information technology sectors. This internship provides hands-on experience with cloud security, federal cybersecurity standards, compliance engineering, security automation, and secure software development while supporting real-world government technology initiatives. Key Responsibilities Assist with implementing, documenting, and validating cybersecurity controls aligned with federal cybersecurity and cloud security best practices. Support security compliance initiatives, including the development and maintenance of security documentation, policies, procedures, and supporting artifacts. Assist in developing and maintaining compliance documentation and structured security artifacts, including OSCAL-based documentation that supports automated compliance and authorization workflows. Support compliance assessments, security reviews, authorization readiness activities, evidence collection, and remediation tracking. Collaborate with software developers and cloud engineers to integrate security and compliance requirements throughout the software development lifecycle. Identify opportunities to automate compliance documentation, evidence collection, and security workflows using Python, APIs, AI, or low-code tools. Support the implementation of cloud security controls across AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform. Assist with vulnerability assessments, security testing, and remediation activities. Continuously learn and apply emerging cybersecurity technologies, compliance standards, and automation techniques to support client engagements. Develop technical documentation, implementation guides, compliance reports, and process documentation. Participate in Agile project activities and collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams. Support DevSecOps initiatives by integrating security and compliance practices into the software development lifecycle. Job Requirements Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, Information Security, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline. 0–2 years of experience through internships, research, assistantships, academic projects, cybersecurity competitions, or technical coursework. Understanding of cybersecurity principles, cloud security, and secure software development. Familiarity with cybersecurity and compliance frameworks such as NIST SP 800-53, NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), FedRAMP, CMMC, CIS Controls, ISO/IEC 27001, or similar standards through coursework, research, or projects. Experience with one or more scripting or programming languages such as Python, PowerShell, Bash, or JavaScript. Strong analytical, documentation, and problem-solving skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team environment. U.S. Citizenship. Preferred Qualifications Coursework, research, or project experience in cloud security, cybersecurity compliance, governance, risk management, or secure software development. Familiarity with security documentation, compliance assessments, or audit preparation. Interest in federal cybersecurity, cloud compliance, or compliance automation. Exposure to OSCAL, security automation, or structured security documentation is a plus. Familiarity with one or more cloud platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform. Experience using Python or scripting languages to automate technical or business processes. Interest in cybersecurity engineering, compliance automation, DevSecOps, cloud security, or federal technology consulting. Security certifications or coursework such as CompTIA Security+, ISC² Certified in Cybersecurity (CC), AWS Cloud Practitioner, or Microsoft Azure Fundamentals are a plus. This role will work closely with leadership and department leads to identify repetitive manual work, convert undocumented processes into clear procedures, and build practical automation solutions using the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. PreferredMicrosoft Power Platform Fundamentals certification, such as PL-900.Experience with Power Apps, Power BI, SharePoint Lists, Power Automate Desktop, Dataverse, or Copilot Studio.Internship, co-op, class project, or work sample involving workflow automation, process improvement, dashboards, apps, or business systems.Basic understanding of SharePoint list and library structures.Experience with ticketing systems, CRM systems, PSA systems, or business operations software.Exposure to process mapping, Lean, Six Sigma, business analysis, or operations improvement.Ability to create simple training guides, checklists, and user instructions. Work Sample or PortfolioCandidates should be prepared to discuss or provide an example of a project they have completed. This may include a class project, an internship project, a personal project, a workflow, an automation, a dashboard, an app, or a process-improvement example. What You’ll GainThis is an opportunity to help shape how a growing technology company operates internally. The person in this role will have direct exposure to leadership, operations, administration, finance, HR, service, and sales support workflows.You will not be working on theoretical projects. You will be building practical solutions that employees use every day. Your work will help reduce manual effort, improve accountability, strengthen documentation, and support the company’s long-term goal of becoming more efficient, automated, and scalable.This internship is designed as a learning and development opportunity and does not guarantee full-time employment upon graduation. jobs.title: Hardware & Automation Test Intern / Junior Engineer at Global ETS
jobs.description: Employer: Global ETS Expires: 08/24/2026 About the RoleWe're an innovative semiconductor testing company looking for a motivated student or junior engineer to help us bridge the gap between hardware reality and modern AI-driven automation. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with our senior engineers, get hands-on exposure to real test-floor operations in an advanced electronics environment, and contribute to the tools and test flows we rely on every single day.This is a learning-first position. More than a perfect resume, we value your curiosity, your attention to detail, and your willingness to get hands-on with both code and hardware.What You'll Work On1. Circuit Theory & Hardware AnalysisThis is the foundation for everything else. You'll use oscilloscopes and multimeters to trace signal integrity issues and perform power analysis, and you'll carry out basic PCB modifications and SMD soldering under the guidance of senior engineers. Our belief: only when you truly understand what the hardware is doing can AI actually help.2. Process Automation via Vibe CodingYou'll use Python to automate parsing test data, cleaning logs, and generating yield reports—but the point isn't hand-crafting every line. It's about driving development through intent, iterating quickly alongside AI, and being able to read, modify, and verify the code the AI produces. The core of coding is shifting from "can you write it" to "can you steer the AI to write it correctly."3. AI Agentic Test FlowsYou'll help the team evaluate and integrate AI development tools so machine learning can accelerate our debugging and test processes, and you'll assist in developing and maintaining ATE (automated test equipment) test programs. Our goal isn't just to have AI answer questions—it's to design agentic pipelines that can autonomously connect to the bench, run tests, and produce reports.What We're Looking ForEnrolled in (or recently graduated from) an Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related program; a solid foundation in Circuit Theory—you should be able to read basic schematics and understand logic gates; comfortable with at least one programming language (Python or C/C++ preferred) as a basis for collaborating with AI; detail-oriented and willing to dig into unfamiliar hardware systems or massive data logs; and genuinely curious about how software directly controls and tests physical hardware in the real world.Nice to HaveHands-on experience with lab equipment (oscilloscopes, multimeters) or basic soldering skills; coursework or project experience with FPGA development (Verilog/VHDL) or digital logic; familiarity with—or strong interest in—integrating AI/ML APIs for data or coding automation.

jobs.title: Innovation Associate at Cortado Group, LLC
jobs.description: Employer: Cortado Group, LLC Expires: 08/27/2026 Innovation Associate (AI-First Solutions)Sit in the customer's chair, name the pain, and ship AI-first solutions: agents, classifiers, analytics, whatever the problem calls for. High EQ and high IQ, in the same person.What this role isYou are here to build AI-first solutions. Products and systems that make painful work disappear for the humans who have to do it. The output will take the form of software, agents, scripts, analytical systems, and whatever we end up calling these things next. The form matters less than the outcome.This is not a build-to-spec role. There is no ticket queue. Your job is to sit in the customer's chair, learn where it hurts, name the pain clearly, and iterate toward solutions that are easy to implement, easy to understand, and deliver real value exactly where the pain is.AI shows up two ways in what you build, and you will learn to operate fluently in both. You use AI as leverage while you build: Claude, Cursor, agent frameworks, and whatever tools the moment calls for. And you use AI as part of the solution itself: conversational analytics, psychometrics, ML, agents that do work humans used to have to do by hand.This is not vibe coding. Vibe coding is prompt-and-pray. AI-fiic, user-centered, and built by people who care more about thecustomer's outcome than about the elegance of their own code.What you will do (responsibilities)- Sit with the user (real clients, real internal operators, real problems) until you understand what hurts and why.- Design solutions that remove the pain with the least possiblo read a manual, you failed.- Match the technique to the problem. LLM, classifier, retrieval, psychometric model, agent, deterministic logic: the right answer is whichever one delivers the outcome.- Build real products that go into real hands. Ship them. Watch them work. Fix what does not.- Contribute to Cortado's internal platforms, agent systems, as we bet the firm on.- Use AI as leverage throughout. Write less code by hand than any engineer before you has written, and ship more of it.Who we are looking for (skills and minimum requirements)This role requires high EQ and high IQ in the same person. That is a rare combination and we are serious about both.- High EQ. You can sit across from a stranger, listen, and actually hear what they are saying, including the part they are not saying out loud. You feel other people's friction. You want to remove it.- High IQ. You can think abstractly, decompose problems, and learn complex technical material quickly. You are comfortable in the space between "I don'tunderstand this yet" and "I understand it now."- You are comfortable being uncomfortable. You are about to be taught things you did not know you did not know.- You have built something, somewhere. A project, a script, a not have to be impressive. It has to be real.- You use AI daily and have opinions about it, even if those opinions are still forming.- You are willing to work through the gauntlet. We hire on evi- 0–3 years of experience. Recent grads welcome. What you will learn How to sit in a customer's chair until you can feel their problem as your own. How to translate that feeling into a solution that is easy to implement, easy to understand, and lands value right where it hurts. How for an LLM, a classifier, a retrieval system, a psychometricmodel, an agent, or plain deterministic code, and how to match the tool to the outcome.Much of what you will learn here is not yet written down anywhere, because the future is actively being invented. You will be part of inventing it.

jobs.title: Data Integration/Engineering Intern at New York City Fire Pension Fund
jobs.description: Employer: New York City Fire Pension Fund Expires: 08/28/2026 The NYC Fire Pension Fund is looking for a Data Integration / Engineering Intern.About the RoleWe are looking for a practical, detail-oriented Data Integration / Engineering Intern to join our team. In this role, you won't need years of industry experience, but you will need strong logical reasoning, a solid grasp of SQL, and a knack for troubleshooting data issues.You will work directly with our data pipelines to help clean, process, and ensure the reliability of our datasets. If you love solving puzzles using the process of elimination and enjoy turning messy data into structured, reliable information, this is a great fit for you. Key ResponsibilitiesData Processing & ETL: Assist in building, maintaining, and monitoring data pipelines to ingest and transform data from multiple sources.Data Quality & Flagging: Identify anomalies, duplicate entries, or missing data. Write logic to flag questionable records for further review without breaking downstream processes.Troubleshooting: Use systematic problem-solving and process of elimination to root-cause why a pipeline failed or why a dataset looks incorrect.Database Maintenance: Write and optimize basic to intermediate SQL queries to analyze, clean, and validate stored data.Documentation: Keep brief, clear notes on data quality rules, flagged record criteria, and pipeline workflows.Communicating: You’ll be engaging office staff in learning about their work habits, how to handle a conversation and working in-person. The primary form of engagement is in-office with emphasis in face-to-face dialogue. You will be presenting work as well to your team members, staff, supervisors and leadership. What We’re Looking ForTechnical SkillsSQL Foundations: Working knowledge of SQL (SELECT, JOINs, GROUP BY, WHERE filtering, CASE statements, and basic aggregations).Data Handling: Basic understanding of data structures (e.g., CSV, JSON, relational tables).Scripting (Bonus): Familiarity with Python, Bash, or another scripting language is a plus, but not required.Mindset & Problem-SolvingProcess of Elimination: Excellent logical reasoning skills—you know how to isolate variables step-by-step to figure out where data is breaking.Attention to Detail: High instinct for spot-checking numbers and catching inconsistencies before they reach production.Common Sense & Ownership: You know when to ask for help, when to double-check your work, and how to apply practical logic to business rules.Curiosity: A natural desire to understand why data looks the way it does.Multiple Priorities: You’ll be exposed to a startup like environment where we all handle multiple projects at the same time given the amount of slack that may manifest itself by resources you might not have control.What You’ll GainHands-on experience with real-world, enterprise-level data integration pipelines and development methodologies.Mentorship from experienced data engineers and analysts.Exposure to modern data stack tools and cloud environments.Practical experience handling large-scale data quality.Confidence in public speaking and presenting.

jobs.title: USDA-ARS Agricultural Data Solutions Internship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 08/29/2026 Application Deadline 9/25/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription *Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis.ARS Office/Lab and Location: An opportunity is currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS) Partnerships for Data Innovations (PDI), an enterprise-level data solutions provider in the National Measurement and Monitoring Innovations Project within the Agroecosystem Management Research Unit (AMRU) in Lincoln, Nebraska. This opportunity may also be remote.The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.PDI supports ARS researchers and stakeholders by providing technical assistance to develop, host, and maintain public-facing custom data solutions such as web-based applications, digital research tools, and software that support the ARS core mission. Services by PDI provide support to our scientists who are highly experienced in their research fields but may not have the technical, information technology (IT), or data science experience to build digital tools that optimize research efficiency and maximize the impact of their ARS research.Research Project: You will collaborate with the Partnerships for Data Innovations (PDI) team to train in the agile and innovative development of customized data solutions that promote collaboration and stewardship of ARS's research data and other knowledge assets. PDI is the only in-house public-facing enterprise-level data solutions provider for ARS scientists. Learning Objectives: You will learn a diversity of technical skillsets to develop, host, and maintain both internal and public-facing custom data solutions such as web-based applications, digital research tools, and software that support the ARS core mission. Specific training may include, but is not limited to, database development, web application development, and software development. You may request a remote training appointment.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Kyle Stoltz (kyle.stoltz@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: September 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of ARS and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Participant Stipend: You will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. The anticipated stipend range is $6,617 - $6,680 monthly.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and ARS. The position offers exposure to hardware design, embedded systems, and compliance testing in industrial environments, ideal for students eager to apply classroom knowledge to real-world projects. PRINCIPLE RESPONSIBILITIES: • Assist with schematic capture and PCB layout using tools such as Altium or Eagle. • Support development and testing of embedded firmware for microcontrollers in C/C++. • Help prototype and validate hardware designs, ensuring proper integration with mechanical components. • Participate in functional and environmental testing (EMC, vibration, shock, climatic). • Provide support for sustaining engineering tasks, including troubleshooting and documentation. • Perform design research for ongoing projects and assist engineers in identifying technical solutions. • Collaborate on complex modification projects to meet custom application needs of key customers. • Learn and execute test protocols in the engineering lab; generate test reports per Engineering SOP. • Complete at least one technical and one business-related independent project; present progress to the executive team. • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on streamlining engineering products or processes. CRITICAL FACTORS FOR SUCCESS • Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical or Electronic Engineering (or related field). • Must possess a GPA of 3.5 or higher. • Familiarity with basic analog/digital circuit concepts. • Exposure to PCB design tools and microcontroller programming through coursework or projects. • Comfortable using common lab equipment (oscilloscopes, power supplies, logic analyzers, debuggers). • Knowledge of embedded C programming IDEs (microcontroller experience is a plus). • Understanding of ultra-low power mixed-signal electronics and industrial automation concepts preferred. • Familiarity with embedded designs (microprocessor, RAM, EEPROM), analog circuit design (Op Amps, Filters, SPICE simulation), and digital circuit design fundamentals. • Strong problem-solving skills and eagerness to learn. PAY RANGE: $22.00 – $26.00 per hour (based on experience and qualifications) WHAT YOU’LL GAIN • Real-world experience in electronics design and embedded systems. • Mentorship from senior engineers. • Opportunity to contribute to global projects and learn industry standards. • Exposure to compliance testing and product development processes. About Barksdale Founded in 1949, Barksdale is a leading manufacturer of precision control products for industrial applications. As part of Crane Co.’s Process Flow Technologies segment, Barksdale specializes in solutions for pressure, temperature, level, and flow control. Our product portfolio includes switches, transducers, valves, regulators, and air suspension systems, serving demanding applications in oil & gas, transportation, and general industrial markets. With headquarters in Los Angeles, California, and operations in Germany, China, and India, Barksdale combines global reach with local expertise. Backed by Crane Co.’s resources and guided by a commitment to innovation and reliability, we deliver engineered solutions that help customers optimize performance and maintain safety in critical environments. For more information, visit www.barksdale.com. About Crane Co Crane Company (NYSE: CR) is a manufacturer of highly engineered industrial products. Founded in 1855, Crane provides products and solutions to customers in the aerospace, defense and space, chemical and petrochemical, water and wastewater, pharmaceutical, and general industrial end markets. The Company operates through two strategic growth platforms: Aerospace & Electronics and Process Flow Technologies. Crane has approximately 7,000 employees across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia. For more information, visit www.craneco.com. Crane Co. reserves the right to change or assign other duties to this position. The statements contained herein reflect general details as necessary to describe the principal functions of this job, the level of knowledge and skill typically required and the scope of accountability and responsibility. These descriptions should not be considered to be all inclusive listings of work requirements. We are looking for a highly motivated, detail oriented, and energetic Assistant Product Manager Intern to support our nuclear spectroscopy and radiation detection line: isotope identification instruments, scintillation detectors, and custom detector assemblies built for national labs, universities, defense programs, and radiation safety organizations.This is a hands-on seat with the product manager and support / sales teams. Our detector business runs on a long supply chain and a deep archive of past builds, and most of the work is turning that archive into fast, defensible answers for customers. Keep the CRM reliable.● Support technical inquiries from customers and from our network of independent sales representatives, and route the hard ones to engineering with the context already assembled.● Understand customer needs and help develop solutions with engineers across BNC detector hardware and analysis software.● Prepare AI assisted proposals, application notes, comparison tables, and short technical videos, and support regional representatives through order completion.● Develop BNC's presence as a thought leader and solution provider across government, academia, and the private sector.● Support competitive analysis, product variation documentation, version control, webinars, and regional events.Preferred qualifications● Bachelor's degree in Physics, Nuclear Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent preferred. We will consider an electronics technician certificate or relevant hands-on experience.● Coursework or lab time in radiation detection is a strong plus: gamma spectroscopy, multichannel analyzers, photomultiplier and SiPM readout, or scintillator materials such as NaI(Tl), LaBr3, CeBr3, LYSO, CLLBC, and GAGG.● Comfort with spreadsheets and data.
